derivation_notes: The fixed tanh crossover is replaced by a sharper low-contrast suppression by squaring the existing contrast-activation factor, representing microcontact/diffusive constriction effects that deactivate transport channels more strongly near equilibrium. This keeps the heat flux odd in T2 - T1, preserves the same large-contrast limit, and changes the constitutive target mapping directly without adding a new state.
change_summary: The assumption of a single tanh-shaped conductance crossover was relaxed to a stronger near-equilibrium suppression law. The successor therefore leaves early high-contrast exchange similar to the parent but bends dT1/dt downward more strongly as |T2-T1| becomes small relative to conductance_deltaT_scale.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The temperature-difference-dependent conductance reduction has a fixed tanh crossover shape with one universal low-contrast scaling.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Real thermal contact often shows a sharper-than-tanh collapse of effective conductance near zero temperature contrast because only a subset of microcontacts or transport channels remain effective close to equilibrium; this changes the low-contrast constitutive shape without introducing a new energy store.

response_change.parent_relation: The interfacial heat flux is an odd, effectively single-regime function of temperature difference: tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale)*(T2 - T1), so after accounting for the mean-temperature and body-1 factors the target depends on |T2-T1| through one fixed saturation shape.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the near-equilibrium conductance transition with a stronger low-contrast suppression consistent with diffusive constriction/microcontact effects, so the target becomes more strongly curved in |T2-T1| near equilibrium while recovering the parent large-contrast behavior at higher |T2-T1|.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding the same initial temperatures and parameters except for the new shape refinement, late-time relaxation near T1≈T2 is slower than the parent predicts, while early-time large-contrast cooling remains close to the parent law.

evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the refined near-equilibrium suppression exponent/shape parameter takes its parent value, or equivalently where the added curvature correction tends to zero so the original tanh-based transition is restored.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Real thermal contact often shows a sharper-than-tanh collapse of effective conductance near zero temperature contrast because only a subset of microcontacts or transport channels remain effective close to equilibrium; this changes the low-contrast constitutive shape without introducing a new energy store.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the target now depends on T1 and T2 through a changed nonlinear contrast-shape, not just a rescaled amplitude or shifted single threshold. The squared activation preserves the large-contrast limit while independently altering near-zero curvature, which a one-scale tanh parent cannot emulate with one shared parameter set.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The temperature-difference-dependent conductance reduction has a fixed tanh crossover shape with one universal low-contrast scaling.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The near-equilibrium contact activation is more strongly suppressed than tanh predicts, consistent with microcontact/channel deactivation, while the same large-contrast conductance limit is retained.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered by replacing the refined suppression factor (tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale))**2 with tanh(Abs(T2 - T1)/conductance_deltaT_scale), i.e. restoring the original single-shape crossover.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Along the same two-body relaxation trajectory, compare segments with large and small |T2-T1|. At large |T2-T1|/conductance_deltaT_scale the child and parent give nearly the same dT1/dt, but once |T2-T1|/conductance_deltaT_scale falls below order unity the child predicts a distinctly smaller |dT1/dt| and a slower final approach to T1=T2. This is a direct change in the scored mapping from observed T1,T2 to dT1/dt, not merely a change in an auxiliary state.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter refit cannot reproduce both regimes across the same admissible trajectories: changing contact_conductance rescales the whole curve, and changing conductance_deltaT_scale shifts the crossover location but still leaves one fixed tanh near-zero curvature. The child preserves the high-contrast asymptote while imposing stronger low-contrast suppression, so one shared parent parameter set cannot match both the early-time and late-time target responses simultaneously.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes one fixed tanh-shaped crossover from weak to strong contact coupling, which imposes a single near-equilibrium curvature for dT1/dt as a function of temperature contrast.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The temperature-difference-dependent conductance reduction has a fixed tanh crossover shape with one universal low-contrast scaling.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Real thermal contact often shows a sharper-than-tanh collapse of effective conductance near zero temperature contrast because only a subset of microcontacts or transport channels remain effective close to equilibrium; this changes the low-contrast constitutive shape without introducing a new energy store.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized single-shape assumption in the existing temperature-difference-dependent conductance. The parent already includes a weak-coupling-to-strong-coupling transition, but it fixes the target mapping dT1/dt versus T1,T2 to one tanh-based phase across the whole trajectory. Vary the instantaneous contrast |T2-T1| along the observed relaxation while holding the same state definitions, energy-conserving two-body setting, and existing mean-temperature/body-1 modifiers fixed. Then compare early times with large |T2-T1| to late times when |T2-T1| is small relative to conductance_deltaT_scale. The child predicts that dT1/dt falls off more steeply near equilibrium than the parent, producing extra curvature in the target mapping and a slower final temperature approach, yet it remains consistent with positive entropy production and correct heat-flow direction because the flux still has the sign of T2-T1. This is a change to the scored target mapping itself, not merely to an auxiliary trajectory, since dT1/dt at the same observed T1,T2 is altered near equilibrium. No new state or input is needed because the omitted effect is a constitutive-shape refinement of an already modeled process, not a missing hidden reservoir. A single refit of the parent's existing amplitudes and scales cannot generally reproduce both the preserved large-contrast behavior and the sharper low-contrast suppression across admissible trajectories, because changing contact_conductance rescales all contrasts and changing conductance_deltaT_scale shifts one onset scale but does not supply an independent near-zero curvature shape.

scenario_text: Consider two finite thermal bodies placed in contact inside an otherwise isolated enclosure. Energy transfer across the contact causes both temperatures to evolve until they coincide, while the bodies remain internally uniform. The target is the instantaneous temperature-change rate of the first body along the coupled trajectory. Heat capacities and contact conductance are fixed baseline properties.
